facts.statement: Attenborosaurus is an extinct genus of pliosaurid that lived in the Early Jurassic in Dorset, England.
facts.quote: Attenborosaurus is an extinct genus of pliosaurid from the Early Jurassic of Dorset, England.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Sir David Attenborough, while the species name honors William Conybeare.
facts.quote: The genus is named after Sir David Attenborough, the species after William Conybeare.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in Charmouth, Dorset, England in 1880 and formally described in 1881.
facts.quote: The original remains of the holotype, specimen, were discovered in Charmouth, Dorset, England in 1880 and was described in 1881.

facts.statement: The original holotype specimen was destroyed in November 1940 during World War II.
facts.quote: This original specimen was housed at the Bristol City Museum and Art Gallery where it stayed until it was destroyed in November 1940, during World War II.

facts.statement: Originally described as Plesiosaurus conybeari by Sollas in 1881, the species was moved to the new genus Attenborosaurus by Bakker in 1993 based on studies of plaster casts.
facts.quote: At first the animal was thought to be another Plesiosaurus species by William Johnson Sollas in 1881, but after studies on the plaster casts made after the remains, Plesiosaurus conybeari was assigned to a new genus (Attenborosaurus) by Robert T. Bakker in 1993.

facts.statement: The holotype individual of Attenborosaurus measured approximately 4.3 meters in length.
facts.quote: The length of the holotype individual was about 4.3 m.

facts.statement: Attenborosaurus was a piscivorous predator, feeding primarily on fish.
facts.quote: Much like other plesiosaurs, it was piscivorous.

facts.statement: Skin impressions suggest the creature had membranous skin without large scales, likely an adaptation to reduce water resistance.
facts.quote: From the skin impression found with the bones, which was later destroyed, it is presumed that the creature had membranous skin, devoid of any significantly large scales, probably for decreasing water resistances.

facts.statement: Fossils of Attenborosaurus were found in Sinemurian strata in Charmouth, Dorset, England.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en estratos del Sinemuriano de Charmouth, Dorset, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: Attenborosaurus is unusual for combining a relatively long neck with a relatively large head.
facts.quote: Lo inusual de este género es que combina un cuello relativamente largo con una cabeza relativamente grande.

facts.statement: Attenborosaurus lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Attenborosaurus is classified within the family Pliosauridae.
The genus Attenborosaurus was established by Bakker in 1993.
